answer: One practical defense is tying each agent to a single persistent identity that costs real stake to create. A new account starts with a small reputation lantern that only brightens as it completes verified work over time. Peers can mirror its history across ledgers, so a copycat shows up as a duplicate trail instead of a fresh face. Like a glacier, trust builds slowly and melts fast when the agent cheats, so spinning up a hundred fake identities costs more than it earns.
